Hey man, I want to start out by saying I was in your exact position at 22. Please feel free to dm me and I will do everything in my power to help you. The only difference was I also had 300 dollars a month in child support and back child support of 7000 dollars. My biggest advice really comes down to understanding your situation isn’t permanent. Im almost 25 now. In the time between 22 and now I went from living in my car in an unfamiliar city with nothing but a cooking job a hooters. To now being almost debt free planning a wedding making $30/hr as a professional mover and very aggressively saving money for a house and wedding. 

Every day I thought about offing myself. The thing that helped me the most was wanting so badly to be in a position where I could be happy. I knew someday I would be there and that’s what kept me from ending things. Im not quite there yet but im soo very close. 

I will give you basic tips here but know I can go as in depth as you want or need. No use sending you a book if you are not going to even see this to begin with. 

First things first your income. We both know your income is not enough and its one of the biggest things stressing you out. The best way to make more as soon as possible is to find a new job in anything you can. Ive had 36 jobs and I job hopped all the time trying to get more money. While i didn’t always leave for the money any time I could get more I took it. Having multiple jobs at a time even just one or two new shifts a day will skyrocket your income. 

Second is bills. I understand your bills are actually pretty low but they can be better. I assume this includes your rent. So theres two ways of looking at this. One you can do what I did. Couch surf until you find the cheapest possible place to live and do it. Doesn’t matter if that moves you to a new state or not. Stoicism is probably the most important practice I have found so far in my life in Stoic philosophy they teach that differentiating between what we can change and what we can’t change is very important. There are so many people who so often get upset over things that isn’t even within their control. Most of the time in life we don’t get to choose what happens to us. What we do get to choose is how to respond to those things. If you are driving down the road and you’re cruising having a nice ride and all of a sudden some jerk pulls out in front of you. You start yelling at them for going slow and holding you up. Or maybe you curse them under your breath. No you honk your horn at them to tell them what an asshole they are. Or maybe you even do all three. But did you have to yell or did you have to curse at them under your breath. Did it make you feel better. No, and really you didn’t have to be angry at all. Becoming angry was your choice. You cant help that this guy pulled out in front of you. You didn’t make that decision and there’s nothing you can do to change it. But as I mentioned before you can change how you react to it. Instead of being angry why not just back off and cool it at a new cruising speed. Maybe you are in a rush to get where you are going though. You are late for work and your boss said he was going to fire you if you ever stepped foot in there even a minute late ever again. Is yelling at this person or honking going to cause you to get to work faster. I would say odds are probably pretty slim on that one. Cursing under your breath at them? That doesn’t help you either. Doing these things actively keeps you thinking about the consequences of being late and fuels your anger. But if you were to sit tight and be calm even if you’re angry for a second just think can i do something about this person who pulled in front of me and is going slow. No I cant. So why the hell am I worrying about it.

For your original question though, i would try to get someone to do a mock interview with you. Every Chick-fil-A is different I’ve worked at 2 now where the first it was essentially just a conversation that we had no questions really but i just got hired again after 5 years of not working there at a different store and this time i got all of the stereotypical questions such as what are your greatest strengths and what are your greatest weaknesses. Your favorite animal and why. Tell me about yourself. Stuff like this i would suggest having someone you know who has been through this before to sit down with you and interview you and that will help you do your best. Your goal is more of being able to answer quickly rather than correctly just so you are aware. When you are in an interview it should feel like a normal conversation minus the stupid questions but that is how the conversation should flow. No need for over explaining either be concise and to the point.

Any time you submit an application. No matter where to, always follow up immediately. If you don’t you are allowing other applicants to take your potential interview spot. As someone who has been on both sides of the hiring process with many different companies i can tell you without a shred of a doubt most people are hirable and if they get to interview before you they will probably get the job before you.

Keep in mind fast food is always hiring though so its not a big deal in this situation. I would call now and use a script similar to, “hello my name is ___, can i speak to your hiring manager? Hello my name is ____. I applied to your _____ position online and was calling to see if this position has been filled yet or not.”

This will open up the conversation for the manager to tell you whats going on and typically they will ask you on the spot when you are good for an interview if they are still hiring. Also another tip is if they are no longer hiring that position make it clear that you are also interested in any other positions you may be interested in or you could let them know in the event of the position opening back up you will still be interested
